paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss of five different models over the course of 140,000 iterations. The x-axis, labeled "#Iteration," is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels spaced by increments of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” is a linear scale ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick intervals of 0.1. A solid red line represents the Vanilla model, which begins with a loss value of approximately 3.4 and decreases to a final loss of approximately 2.45 over the course of the iterations. A dashed orange line indicates the StrmLLM (n=64) model, starting at a loss around 3.4 and converging to a final loss of approximately 2.60. Several colored lines represent the SepLLM models; a green line represents SepLLM (n=64), starting at approximately 3.4 and ending at around 2.52; a magenta line represents SepLLM (n=64, H/T), beginning at approximately 3.4 and converging to a loss of approximately 2.49; a turquoise line represents SepLLM (n=128), starting at approximately 3.4 and settling at a final loss of approximately 2.55.
